decision: Add type="ws" as an inbound transport for channels.<name> and mount it on the existing hive serve listener at a fixed route derived from the channel key: /channel/websocket/<name>. The path is not a config field and a path key is rejected; there is no custom or shared path. Reuse the existing hive-channel/1 JSON-RPC methods and SessionBackend semantics, authenticate each connection with a channel-specific bearer token, and allow exactly one active connection per channel. stdio entries remain the default and are unchanged.
goal_beyond_request: Make a channel implementable in any language that has a WebSocket and JSON client, without putting a process on the Hive host, while keeping the existing stdio channel path and its upstream-compatible session semantics intact. The channel becomes a remote peer of the same ChannelHost contract instead of a Go-specific child process.

feasibility.verdict: 可行，但不是按当前配置示例原样可行。
feasibility.why: The current host is process-oriented: every enabled channels entry must have command/args, Host.Start spawns one stdio child, and Host.handlePluginRequest is only reachable from that child. The example has type=ws, no command, and no route, so today it would be reported failed with 'no command configured'. There is also no WebSocket route in hive serve and no WebSocket server dependency in go.mod. The protocol layer, however, is already a transport-neutral JSON-RPC contract, so the work is an inbound transport adapter plus route/auth/lifecycle work, not a new session model.
current_limits: internal/channels/config.go PluginConfig has Name, Enabled, Command, Args, Cwd, Env and Section; it does not read type or path.
internal/channels/host.go startOne requires Argv(); an enabled entry with no command is failed, as the existing nocommand test proves.
There is no /channel/websocket route; internal/server/app.go registers API routes and a GET / SPA fallback, and go.mod has no WebSocket server module.
internal/channels/subscription.go hard-codes *pluginProcess in delivery; the output path needs a transport-neutral sink.
internal/server/app.go desktopAuth checks every path except /api/queen-mail/ when HIVE_DESKTOP_TOKEN is set; channel auth must not piggyback on it.
hello carries the whole config section and an absolute state_dir, while Output.Files carries absolute host paths; those are not usable by a remote language client.
reusable_parts: hive-channel/1 JSON-RPC envelopes and method names in internal/channels/protocol.go.
Host.handlePluginRequest and the SessionBackend interface, which already wrap open_session, send, subscribe, unsubscribe, set_title and judge.
Output kinds, subscription queue, drop-oldest policy and seq gaps in internal/channels/subscription.go.

problem.statement: A channel is currently a local implementation detail: the server owns the child process, the child talks JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout, and the plugin must run on the same host to read files and state. That is not language-neutral for remote implementations and it does not give a remote client a real-time duplex link. A WebSocket endpoint is the natural transport, but the existing config example does not describe the identity, path, authentication, lifecycle or file semantics needed to make it safe.
user_value: Any language with a WebSocket client can implement a channel; no Go process, no stdin framing, no child lifecycle.
The server can push message, question, error, files and idle outputs in real time over the same socket.
The existing session methods and queen semantics stay identical, so a port is a transport port rather than a second channel model.
The stdio wxbot path remains the default and needs no migration.
The route is opt-in and can be mounted without a second port or a separate daemon.
problem.why_not_now: This is a Go-only extension; upstream Hive exposes channel plugins as in-process packages and has no WebSocket channel transport. It must stay at design status until path, auth, attachment and single-connection decisions are accepted.

protocol.name: Hive channel JSON-RPC
protocol.framing: one UTF-8 JSON object per text message; binary messages are rejected; no NDJSON

requirements.statement: Mount an opt-in WebSocket channel route on the existing hive serve listener; do not add a second port or a separate daemon.
requirements.acceptance: A configured ws entry is reachable on the same host/port as /api/health; no listener is opened for the channel.

requirements.statement: Extend channels.<name> with type=stdio|ws. type defaults to stdio; command/args/cwd/env remain the stdio path; ws must not require a command or spawn a process.
requirements.acceptance: The existing wxbot section is unchanged; an enabled ws entry with no command mounts; an enabled stdio entry without command still fails as before.

requirements.statement: Each ws channel has exactly one route derived from its configuration key: /channel/websocket/<name>. The path is not configurable; a path key is rejected, and a shared path cannot select among several channels.
requirements.acceptance: The derived route works for each valid name; a path key, duplicate route, invalid name or traversal string is a startup error; a client cannot select another channel by path.

requirements.statement: Authenticate every ws connection with a channel-specific bearer token, bound to the configured channel; do not reuse HIVE_DESKTOP_TOKEN and never put the token in the URL.
requirements.acceptance: Missing, wrong, cross-channel and query/path tokens fail before upgrade; a valid token works; logs contain no token.

requirements.statement: Reuse hive-channel/1 JSON-RPC envelopes, hello/start handshake, request ids, error kinds and output notifications; do not invent an MCP or a second channel semantic model.
requirements.acceptance: The server sends hello then start; a client responds welcome then start result; malformed versions and unknown methods return typed errors.

requirements.statement: Expose exactly the existing client-to-host methods open_session, send, subscribe, unsubscribe, set_title and judge, with the same params and result shapes as stdio.
requirements.acceptance: Method tests use the same fixtures as the stdio host; no new channel method becomes available to a model or to a remote client.

requirements.statement: Keep Output kinds, per-subscription ordering, seq gaps and the bounded drop-oldest queue; do not let a slow WebSocket client block the event bus.
requirements.acceptance: message/question/error/files/idle arrive in order; a full queue increments drops and leaves a visible seq gap; the backend remains responsive.

requirements.statement: Do not send absolute host paths to a remote ws client. Output attachments use opaque file_refs and an authenticated download route, or the channel explicitly returns an unsupported-attachment error.
requirements.acceptance: Output.Files is not exposed as a host path on ws; file_refs resolve only inside the session attachment root; traversal and oversized files fail closed.

requirements.statement: Define a bounded connection lifecycle: one active connection per channel, handshake/start timeouts, ping/pong liveness, close codes and cleanup of every subscription on disconnect.
requirements.acceptance: A second connection is refused or replaces the first according to config; a silent peer is closed after the pong deadline; disconnect unsubscribes all sessions.

requirements.statement: Report ws channel state alongside existing channels: state running/off/failed, transport, connected, connection count and last_error, without breaking the existing GET /api/channels fields.
requirements.acceptance: Configured/disconnected/connected/failed transitions are visible; existing stdio channel entries keep their current shape.

requirements.statement: Redact secrets and host-only state from hello: omit state_dir and token material, expose only a safe config projection, validate Origin when present and require TLS for remote use.
requirements.acceptance: A captured hello has no token, no environment value and no absolute state_dir; browser Origin mismatch is rejected; plaintext remote use is documented as unsupported.

requirements.statement: Keep the pure-Go, CGO_ENABLED=0 release boundary. A new WebSocket dependency requires explicit approval; otherwise implement the minimal RFC 6455 server with the standard library.
requirements.acceptance: CGO=0 builds/tests pass; the dependency decision is recorded; no cgo or bundled runtime is added.

requirements.statement: Preserve the existing stdio channel path, configuration shape and upstream-compatible session semantics; ws is an additive transport, not a migration.
requirements.acceptance: The wxbot stdio host still starts; stdio protocol fixtures are byte-identical; no existing channel config needs editing.

requirements.statement: Publish a language-neutral wire contract with Python and Node examples and a fake-client conformance harness.
requirements.acceptance: Two independent clients complete handshake and one open_session/send/subscribe round trip against a fake backend; missing clients remain an external gap.

non_goals: Do not add a second HTTP listener, a sidecar daemon or an external WebSocket proxy requirement.
Do not expose MCP semantics or MCP tools through this endpoint; this is the channel host protocol.
Do not add Hive-to-Hive federation, remote channel discovery or a second identity store.
Do not add hot reload; configuration is read at serve startup like the current channels section.
Do not support multiple active plugin connections for one channel in v1; one bot identity, one connection.
Do not add replay, an inbox or a cursor in v1; a disconnected client must re-open and re-subscribe.
Do not add channel tools to the local model tool catalogue.
Do not change the stdio child protocol or the existing wxbot configuration contract.
assumptions: The Hive process is the server; a language client is the channel plugin and connects to /channel/websocket/<name>.
The endpoint is off unless an enabled ws entry exists; no command is spawned for a ws entry.
A channel token is supplied through an environment variable named by token_env and is never printed.
The ws client can send an Authorization header. Browser clients that cannot set one need a same-origin BFF or a cookie design; that is an open decision.
Remote deployment terminates TLS at a trusted reverse proxy and uses wss; plaintext remote WebSocket is unsupported.
The client accepts at-most-once output semantics with seq gaps and re-subscribes after reconnect; durable delivery is a later feature.
The channel client owns its local state; an absolute server state_dir is neither useful nor safe to send.

options.name: type=ws route on the existing hive serve listener, reusing hive-channel/1
options.reason: Matches the user request, gives language-neutral real-time transport, avoids a second port and keeps the session backend and protocol vocabulary. Requires a new inbound transport adapter and auth, not just a config field.

options.name: Separate WebSocket listener on a dedicated port
options.reason: The request explicitly says to share hive serve; a second port adds deployment, discovery, proxy and state-sync surface for no protocol benefit.

options.name: Keep stdio and run a local WebSocket-to-stdio bridge process
options.reason: Still requires a process on the Hive host; the remote language client would depend on a Go bridge and the host would still own the child lifecycle.

options.name: Adopt an approved pure-Go WebSocket library instead of hand-rolling RFC 6455
options.reason: The library is safer and shorter, but it changes go.mod and needs explicit approval under the no-new-dependency rule. The transport contract is independent of this choice.

options.name: Expose MCP over WebSocket instead of the channel JSON-RPC
options.reason: MCP is an agent/tool protocol, not the ChannelHost object model. Reusing MCP would create a second session/tool layer and break the existing channel semantics.

options.name: One shared /channel/websocket/ path for every channel
options.reason: The path alone cannot identify the configured channel or its token. A later subprotocol or first-frame selector is possible, but it makes pre-upgrade 404/401/403 impossible and increases ambiguity.

D1.title: Route placement
D1.text: Mount one handler per enabled ws entry at /channel/websocket/<name> on the existing http.Server. Register the route before the GET / SPA fallback. The handler upgrades only after path, token and Origin checks; the route is not under /api and does not inherit the desktop token policy. No second listener is opened.

D2.title: Configuration and validation
D2.text: Extend PluginConfig with Type (stdio default), TokenEnv, AllowedOrigins, MaxConnections, Takeover and timeout/limit fields. Parse type before the stdio command checks. For ws, do not require command, do not spawn a process, validate the name and derive the route as /channel/websocket/<name>; a path key is rejected. Require token_env and a unique route. Invalid entries are startup failures, not silent disables. Read at serve startup; changing an entry requires restart.

D3.title: Authentication and connection identity
D3.text: The client sends an Authorization header with the bearer scheme; the token is read from token_env. The server compares in constant time, binds the token to the configured channel name and rejects a token presented on another channel. Missing/wrong token is 401/403 before 101. If Origin is present it must match allowed_origins; native clients without Origin are allowed only with a valid token. HIVE_DESKTOP_TOKEN is never accepted as a channel token and the token never appears in the URL, query string or hello config.

D4.title: Wire protocol
D4.text: Use WebSocket text frames carrying one UTF-8 JSON-RPC 2.0 object each. Negotiate subprotocol hive-channel/1 during the upgrade. Reuse hello, start, output, open_session, send, subscribe, unsubscribe, set_title and judge exactly as internal/channels/protocol.go defines them. Binary frames are rejected. No MCP methods and no per-channel custom model are introduced.

D5.title: Backend and request reuse
D5.text: The ws transport calls the same request dispatcher as the stdio host instead of duplicating session logic. Extract the unexported handler behind a small handler/sink seam so both transports share open_session, send, subscribe, unsubscribe, set_title and judge. The channel backend remains SessionBackend; the ws layer must not import internal/server, internal/cli or internal/tools/builtin.

D6.title: Lifecycle and close semantics
D6.text: States are CONNECTED, HELLO_SENT, START_SENT, READY and CLOSED. After 101 the server sends hello (id srv-1); the client must answer within handshake_timeout_seconds; the server sends start (id srv-2); the client answers; only then are client requests accepted. A request before READY gets -32000 with kind not_ready. On stop, send a bounded stop request then close 1001. Disconnect closes every subscription and releases the channel slot.

D7.title: Output and backpressure
D7.text: Reuse Output and outputParams. Each subscription has one ordered queue of queue_size and one writer; when the queue is full, drop the oldest output, increment drops and let seq gaps tell the client. A slow ws peer must never block the event bus. v1 is at-most-once: no replay buffer and no cursor. Reconnect means open_session/subscribe again.

D8.title: Remote attachments
D8.text: For ws, do not expose Output.Files as absolute host paths. Add an optional file_refs array with an opaque id, name, size, mime and sha256; the client downloads through an authenticated GET /channel/artifacts/<id> route scoped to the session attachment root. Input send.images stays the existing base64 form. If attachment transfer is not accepted, v1 must return a typed unsupported_attachment error instead of a useless path.

D9.title: State and observability
D9.text: Extend GET /api/channels entries for ws with transport=ws, connected, connections and last_error while keeping name and state. state is off when disabled, running when the route is mounted, failed on config/auth/listener errors. Logs contain channel name, connection generation, close code and counts, never Authorization, token, text or attachment bytes.

D10.title: Limits and liveness
D10.text: Enforce max_frame_bytes before JSON decode; reject binary frames; no permessage-deflate; require masked client frames; send ping every ping_interval_seconds and require pong within pong_timeout_seconds; bound in-flight requests and handshake time. One active connection per channel by default. These are transport checks, not new channel semantics.

D11.title: Hello redaction and remote safety
D11.text: Build the hello config from a safe projection: enabled, type, path and non-secret plugin options only. Omit state_dir for ws and omit token_env's value, Authorization, env values and absolute paths. Validate the channel name before joining it to the route. Remote use must be wss behind a trusted proxy; do not bind 0.0.0.0 as a shortcut and do not reuse the desktop token.

D12.title: Package and dependency boundary
D12.text: Keep the transport-neutral protocol and host seam in internal/channels (ws_*.go in the same package is acceptable to reuse unexported helpers); mount it from a thin server adapter. Do not import internal/server, internal/cli or internal/tools/builtin from the channel transport. The default choice is a minimal standard-library RFC 6455 server; the approved-library option is recorded in O4 and needs explicit dependency approval before code.

identity_contract.channel: The route name and token are the channel identity; the token may not be presented on another channel.
identity_contract.client: The client is a channel plugin, not a model user and not a desktop browser; it never supplies from_queen or an authorization role.
identity_contract.token: Authorization header only; token_env names the source; no URL/query token and no HIVE_DESKTOP_TOKEN.
identity_contract.hello: Contains name, protocol and a redacted config projection; never state_dir or token material.
identity_contract.session: session_id is returned by open_session and is the only key used by send/subscribe/unsubscribe/set_title.
identity_contract.files: file_refs ids are opaque and scoped to the channel/session; absolute host paths are not disclosed.

risks.risk: The derived /channel/websocket/<name> URL is not what an existing client expects
risks.impact: a remote client cannot connect with a custom path
risks.mitigation: document the one canonical route; do not add a path key; a future shared-path selector needs its own pre-upgrade identity design and tests.

risks.risk: A hand-written RFC 6455 server has parser/security bugs
risks.impact: invalid frames, DoS or protocol confusion
risks.mitigation: keep the frame subset minimal, test masking/fragmentation/close/ping, fuzz frames, and prefer an approved library if the dependency gate opens.

risks.risk: The ws route is outside /api and bypasses desktopAuth
risks.impact: a new unauthenticated route on a remotely bound server
risks.mitigation: mandatory per-channel token, Origin check, TLS boundary and a startup refusal when token_env is absent.

risks.risk: Remote clients cannot read absolute Output.Files paths
risks.impact: images/documents silently break or leak host paths
risks.mitigation: file_refs + authenticated download, or a typed unsupported_attachment error; never send host paths.

risks.risk: At-most-once output with drop-oldest loses real replies
risks.impact: a slow or disconnected channel misses messages
risks.mitigation: document seq gaps; resubscribe after reconnect; durable inbox/replay is a later design.

risks.risk: hello carries the whole configuration section
risks.impact: tokens, env values or absolute paths leak to a remote client
risks.mitigation: build a safe config projection and omit state_dir for ws; test captured hello.

risks.risk: Single active connection becomes a reconnect race
risks.impact: two clients write to one channel or a reconnect is refused
risks.mitigation: generation ids, explicit takeover policy and a test for both refusal and replacement.

open_questions: Should the server be hand-written on net/http Hijacker (no dependency) or use an approved pure-Go WebSocket library? O4 is deferred until dependency approval.
How should a browser client authenticate, given that the WebSocket API cannot set an Authorization header? A same-origin BFF/cookie design is different from the native-client header path.
Is file transfer in v1 required? If yes, choose file_refs plus an authenticated GET /channel/artifacts/<id>; if no, v1 must return a typed unsupported_attachment error for Output.Files.
What is the second-connection policy: reject with 409, or replace the old connection with close 4004? The default proposal is reject; takeover needs an explicit config.
Should a mounted ws route with no connected client report state running (endpoint ready) or off? The proposed contract keeps state=running and adds connected=false.
Do you need replay/inbox/at-least-once delivery? The current design is at-most-once with seq gaps and no cursor, because the existing channel queue is drop-oldest.
